newsitem.title: CHINA: China province ends random fees on foreigners.
newsitem.headline: China province ends random fees on foreigners.

text.p: China's northeastern Liaoning province has canceled 118 separate random fees worth a total of more than 300 million yuan ($3.6 billion) being charged without authorisation to foreign investors.
The move to scrap the arbitrary, unauthorised fees was aimed at improving the region's investment environment, the Xinhua news agency on Wednesday quoted vice-governor Gao Guozhu as saying.
Liaoning has so far approved the establishment of more than 14,600 overseas-funded enterprises, with contractual foreign investment exceeding $20 billion.

The province found more than 1,000 government organisations engaged in the random fee collection in a huge check on the collection of fees on overseas-funded enterprises between April and August last year, Gao said.
"The provincial government has realised that arbitrary fees have tarnished Liaoning's image and will dampen investor interest in our province," he was quoted as saying.
"We're determined to wipe out all unreasonable and illegal fees for overseas investors," Gao said.
Much foreign investment in the province comes from Japan and South Korea.
